messages:
Maya: heads-up — the prefix-hit dashboard shows a sudden drop for redwood-lite on /api/chat between 2026-04-02T01:05 and 01:25 UTC. tokens-saved down ~720k across multiple tenants.
Leo: any recent kernel or batching flips around then? that scale often tracks a rollout.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: kernel-selection:v4 canary -> 20% at 2026-04-02T00:58:12Z; batch-split:heuristic=BETA toggled at 2026-04-02T01:03:45Z
Rachel: I compared the per-route hit curves. The biggest delta is for short/prompt-style routes (/api/chat, /widget/compose) not long-context completes.
Tom: I sampled KV traces for that window. KV miss rate for redwood-lite on /api/chat jumped from ~10% to ~31%. The key-extractor is seeing token-offset deltas after the kernel change.
Maya: snippet from the dashboard query (top rows):
```
route        | model         | hit_before -> hit_after | tokens_delta
/api/chat    | redwood-lite  | 18% -> 6%              | -0.72M
/widget/compose | redwood-pro | 46% -> 44%             | -0.09M
/inbox/summary  | redwood-lite | 25% -> 13%             | -0.4M
```
Leo: sounds like two interacting factors: kernel-selection v4 changes byte->token mapping in folded kernels; batch-split heuristic changes where we cut sequences for key derivation. Together they shift canonical keys.
Rachel: profiler evidence: in several samples the kernel used a different tokenizer path, which produced a different normalization of punctuation -> keys diverged.
Tom: minimal reproducer I pasted to perf-bucket shows the same: when kernel picks alt-tokenizer, key computed on token offsets moves 1-2 tokens. Example: 
```
orig: "List the steps:
 1) init
 2) run"
old_key: "list_steps|1) init 2) run"
new_key: "list_steps|1)
 init 2) run"
```
Maya: mitigation options:
- rollback kernel-selection:v4 on canary hosts immediately
- deploy a tolerant key-compare for keys < 48 tokens (case/space/linebreak tolerant) to canary only
- run targeted warmups for top impacted tenant/model/route combos
Leo: low-risk first step: deploy tolerant compare to canary. If that restores hit-rate we keep batch-split on and iterate on kernel-selection.
Rachel: dashboard work items:
- add per-tenant token-saved sparkline to the heatmap hover
- surface active canary flag combinations in the time-range header (so ops can correlate flags to anomalies)
- add a kernel-selection dimension to the heatmap (kernel variant as series)
- create alert: single-tenant tokens-lost > 250k in 30m OR route-model combo loss > 500k in 1h
Tom: profiler run command I used:
```
/run-profile --model redwood-lite --route /api/chat --duration 30m --kv-sample=0.35 --kernels=all --capture-tokenmap
```
perf-bot: perf-bot: profile artifacts uploaded to s3://perf-artifacts/1788888888/redwood-lite-kernprof.tar.gz
Maya: runbook (short):
1) Leo -> push tolerant key-compare to canary (10% hosts) and monitor heatmap for 30m
2) Rachel -> add per-tenant sparkline and kernel dimension to heatmap dashboard (small PR)
3) Tom -> run full profiler + KV trace set and flag top mismatches (already running)
4) if tolerant compare fails, rollback kernel-selection:v4 on canary (Maya)
Leo: also note: we should add an offline CI test that runs sample prompts under kernel variants and diffs derived keys. That would catch cross-kernel key drift before canary. Filing that RFC after we stabilize.
Rachel: agreed. For observability short-term I'll wire the hover to include token-saved per-tenant and a small CTA to warmup the top impacted combos.
Tom: uploading KV diffs now. Once we have warmup results we'll reprofile and decide whether kernel-selection needs a revert or a deeper normalization change (decouple key derivation from kernel-specific offsets).
Maya: thanks — good triage. tagging @pm-sarah and @cs-team to prep comms for any affected customers. We'll reconvene in 40m after the canary patch and warmups. :thumbsup:
Leo: starting the canary tolerant-compare rollout now :hourglass:
Maya: (later) canary tolerant-compare at 10% restored ~60% of the lost tokens in the next 25m. Tom's reprofile will confirm remaining mismatches.
